summary: monogrok: heavily obfuscated spam / SMTP-cracker / phishing operator toolkit
details: Package ships as a CLI (`bin: monogrok`, `main: oibWljdTg.js`, homepage https://mntmc.rip) with no npm lifecycle scripts. All ~250 JavaScript sources are packed with javascript-obfuscator (RC4-decoded string arrays, self-defense regex traps, hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x65a07a`). The module tree is an offensive-mailing / operator toolkit: `func/smx/*` performs SMTP credential cracking against operator-supplied targets (SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES helpers), `func/emx/*` performs email address extraction and enrichment, `func/sho/*` builds Shodan queries for exposed relays, `func/ipr/*` rotates SOCKS/HTTP proxies, `func/rdr/*` builds redirect chains, `func/box/*` targets mailbox harvesting (Gmail/Outlook IMAP/EWS/OWA, cookie configs), and `_init/props/.smtp/resulthook.txt` contains a Discord result hook template that the operator configures. All harmful capability is directed at external targets that the operator selects at explicit CLI invocation — there are no install/postinstall hooks, no import-time reads of installer secrets (`~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.npmrc`, browser stores), no hardcoded exfiltration of installer data to an author endpoint, and no backdoor into the installer host. Installing or loading the package does not by itself compromise the installer. The package's purpose (spam/cracking operator tooling) is highly likely to violate npm's acceptable-use policy, but under this system's threat model (installer-side attacker benefit or install/import-time destruction) it does not constitute a supply-chain attack on developers who install it.
